answer: A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, which means it forfeits the mesa fee twice and still divides one payout. Because the grove ledger attributes every share, the lagoon audit reveals the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 67% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. That is 5 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
